text: You've got your ticket, luggage checked, and you're all set for that dream vacation. You just need to get there on time.
But at the gate, it's a madhouse. So many people. A long, slow line, and a growing sense of dread.
How can this be? Did the airline make a huge mistake? Did they simply sell too many tickets by accident?
No accident. Airlines *intentionally* overbook flights. They use complex data models to predict exactly how many passengers won't show.
The goal is simple: ensure every flight leaves completely full, maximizing profit. Most of the time, their predictions are right.
But sometimes, everyone shows up. And that's when someone, often you, pays the real price for their invisible system. Now you see it.
